scope: Nozomu Kazama's Kokkuri-san route in kazama.ks.

entries.role: Storyteller and third-year high school student from Kumamoto
entries.note: Showy and teasing. Treat his assurances about the ritual as dialogue, with his confidence and timing intact.
Kazama uses the same name for the practice and the being it calls. He describes the conventional ritual with a ten-yen coin before proposing a five-hundred-yen coin.
Use Kazama's stated term for the Western equivalent.
The unusual source spelling at 4614 appears to describe an unidentified minor spirit. The series glossary uses 雑霊 in its explanation of Kokkuri-san. Preserve Kazama's uncertainty and supply no name.

entries.role: Name Kazama reads from the coin's motion
entries.note: Use the established Latin spelling Aim. The series glossary links this Kiwame appearance with the Aim of The Cat's Paw. The present scene confirms the spoken name and Kazama's unfamiliarity. Gender and identity are left unstated here.

entries.ja: こっくり…こっくり…こっくりさん
entries.en: Nod… nod… Kokkuri-san, the nodding spirit.
entries.note: Kazama points to the bored storytellers nodding off and calls that seeing Kokkuri-san. The English renders the literal nodding sense in the same field.
The coin first spells tama, which Kazama takes to mean balls. Shii completes tamashii, soul. Preserve the partial readings on the board and Kazama's two successive interpretations in speech.
The board stops partway through akai hitsuji, red sheep. Kazama's fragmented chant then supplies sheep, sacrifice and baa. The English caption and ED033 keep the same incompleteness.
Kazama intentionally gets Hosoda's name wrong with a fat/thin surname joke. This local insult at5876 is distinct from the approved name Tomoharu Hosoda.
